judgment.notes: Ω is exactly the positive-time domain, open in the ambient Euclidean product. It adds no smoothness or PDE premise.

Componentwise coordinate derivatives and their order are explicit. The germ/zero-extension convention does not assert global smoothness of the extension; derivatives are used in Ω, with H002 or N001 supplying existence. No regularity of the normal scalar is introduced.

The Laplacian is the finite sum of pure spatial second derivatives, componentwise, with the original sign and no time derivative. The differentiability qualification is explicit and supplied by smoothness when used.

The real density is exactly the two original squared Euclidean terms, with the spatial Frobenius sum and coefficient one. H002 is an explicit guard and direct input to all R using this definition; integrability and regularity are not granted by the definition.

E is defined on positive times by a total integral, so its definition does not presuppose finiteness. N002 separately exports integrability, and N003 explicitly identifies differentiation of the actual finite integral. H002 remains a direct guard input. No time-zero value is asserted in the target; the later auxiliary extension is scoped to the source application.

Lebesgue measure has the original standard coordinate normalization, with the finite product interpretation explicit. The zero-dimensional convention makes the n=1 coordinate split meaningful. Indicator notation is total for arbitrary sets; integrability is not inferred without measurability/finite-measure arguments. Coordinate splitting is supported by M010 rather than a hidden project result.

The dot product is a fully bound finite Euclidean sum in arbitrary finite dimension; the norm-square convention agrees with the original Euclidean energy. It introduces no tangency property; tangency is an N001 conclusion.
